title: Outpatient surgery from the patient’s perspective: perceptions of continuity of care and social vulnerability during postoperative recovery
summary: An increasing number of operations are being carried out on an outpatient basis. As a result, patients spend most of their recovery time at home and have to organise some of their own care. At the same time, contact with healthcare professionals is often limited following the procedure. The study therefore examines how patients experience their care and recovery following outpatient orthopaedic surgery. The focus is on the organisation and continuity of care, the availability of contact persons, and support from family, friends or other significant others. The study also examines which organisational, personal and social circumstances may influence recovery. To this end, adults who have undergone outpatient surgery are surveyed online on two occasions: the day after the operation and one week later. The aim of the study is to gain insights into how postoperative care can be improved from the patient’s perspective.

interventions.name: Adult patients who have undergone outpatient orthopaedic surgery are surveyed via an online questionnaire at two points in time following their operation (1 day and 7 days after the operation)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Scheduled orthopaedic day surgery
Exclusion criteria:
Admission to hospital
sponsor: Institut für Medizinische Informatik, Biometrie und Epidemiologie (IMIBE), Unitversität Duisburg-Essen
